input.answer:
A 36-year-old woman presents with recurrent severe orthostatic headache, photophobia, tremor, and dizziness, three days after discharge following a prior admission in which CSF showed lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated protein, and she received nine days of IV dexamethasone.

**Post-dural puncture CSF leak:** The orthostatic pattern is classic for low CSF pressure following lumbar puncture, which was performed during the prior admission. Limitation: timing of LP relative to headache onset is unclear. Next: confirm orthostatic component on exam; consider MRI brain (pachymeningeal enhancement, sagging) or CT myelogram.

**Ongoing or recurrent CNS inflammation/infection:** CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (83.3 mg/dL) indicate an inflammatory or infectious process. Persistent photophobia and new tremor/dizziness suggest incomplete resolution. Limitation: no MRI or blood results available; specific aetiology unconfirmed. Next: repeat LP, MRI brain with contrast, targeted serologies.

**Dexamethasone withdrawal or adverse effect:** Prolonged steroid use followed by abrupt cessation can cause rebound symptoms, though the orthostatic pattern is atypical. Less likely as sole explanation.

**Reassessment needed:** Confirm true orthostatic component, full neurological exam, and clarify whether headache preceded or followed the LP before deciding management.

A 36-year-old woman presents with recurrent severe orthostatic headache, photophobia, tremor, and dizziness, three days after discharge following a prior admission in which CSF showed lymphocytic pleocytosis and elevated protein, and she received nine days of IV dexamethasone.

**Post-dural puncture CSF leak:** The orthostatic pattern is classic for low CSF pressure following lumbar puncture, which was performed during the prior admission. Limitation: timing of LP relative to headache onset is unclear. Next: confirm orthostatic component on exam; consider MRI brain (pachymeningeal enhancement, sagging) or CT myelogram.

**Ongoing or recurrent CNS inflammation/infection:** CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis (183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (83.3 mg/dL) indicate an inflammatory or infectious process. Persistent photophobia and new tremor/dizziness suggest incomplete resolution. Limitation: no MRI or blood results available; specific aetiology unconfirmed. Next: repeat LP, MRI brain with contrast, targeted serologies.

**Dexamethasone withdrawal or adverse effect:** Prolonged steroid use followed by abrupt cessation can cause rebound symptoms, though the orthostatic pattern is atypical. Less likely as sole explanation.

**Reassessment needed:** Confirm true orthostatic component, full neurological exam, and clarify whether headache preceded or followed the LP before deciding management.
